providers.title: Label Cover instances with value one or small value
providers.scope: Assume the hypotheses (PCP) and (PR). For every sigma > 0 there are finite answer sets and a polynomial-time map from 3-CNF formulas to Label Cover instances (a list of tests, each with a left question, a right question and a map of the answers) with value 1 if the formula is satisfiable and value at most sigma otherwise.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The link distance
providers.scope: The least total length of a sequence of links (sup circle distance inside a copy, length 0 between x and its pullback along a test) is symmetric, satisfies the triangle inequality, is at most the sup distance inside a copy, and is preserved by the half shift.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The graph of a satisfiable instance has a proper coloring with three colors
providers.scope: If all tests of the Label Cover instance can be satisfied, the first branch does not occur and the graph of the reduction has a proper coloring with three colors: the phase of the location at the satisfying answers changes by at least 3/8 along every edge.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Odd Lipschitz extension from a finite set
providers.scope: A function with values in [-1,1] on a finite subset of T^M that is invariant under the half shift, L-Lipschitz for the sup distance and odd, extends to a function on T^M with the same properties.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Decomposition of a function by means over coordinates
providers.scope: f is the sum of the pairwise orthogonal functions f_A (apply Q_i for i in A and E_i for i outside A); Q_i f is the sum of the f_A with i in A, and the mean over the coordinates outside S is the sum of the f_A with A inside S.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Two bounds on influences that do not depend on the number of coordinates
providers.scope: For L and eps there are beta > 0 and K such that every L-Lipschitz H: T^n -> [-1,1] (sup distance) with mean 0 and mean square > eps has a coordinate with influence at least beta, and at most K coordinates have influence at least beta/2; beta and K do not depend on n. The proof uses Austin's junta theorem, which is proved in the course Hypercontractivity on a torus and juntas for Lipschitz functions.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The function of an independent set
providers.scope: For an independent set with the set A of locations, f = e - e o T with e = (1 - 32 dist(., A))_+ has values in [-1,1], is odd, equals 1 on A, is constant across links of length 0 and is 64-Lipschitz inside every copy.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Compatibility along a chain
providers.scope: For the fixed odd 64-Lipschitz extensions F_i along a chain: |F_j(x) - F_i(x o pi_ij)| <= 64/D for i <= j and all x in T^(M_j).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Bounded lists of a set of layers
providers.scope: For a set I of at most s layers there are lists S_I^j of rotations with total size at most d = J(64s,gamma)(m+1)^s such that for every choice of coefficients the function h_(I,t) is within gamma in L^2 of a function of the listed rotations; the lists are determined by the tuple of the least layer and the maps to the other layers of I.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Lists of separated sets of layers are disjoint with high probability
providers.scope: If the value of the instance is at most sigma and max I < min J, the lists A_I and A_J in the last layer meet with probability at most d^2 sigma over the chain.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The alignment theorem
providers.scope: For s, d >= 1 and eta > 0 there are r >= s and a rational law on the s-subsets of [r] such that for every family of lists of size at most d, indexed by the nonempty sets of at most s elements of [r], with A_I and A_J disjoint whenever max I < min J, a random s-set B is bad with probability at most eta; B is not bad if every label can be given an element of B that lies in every I inside B on whose list the label stands. Proved in the following lesson.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Alignment for s = 3 with an explicit law
providers.scope: For s = 3 and r >= 4, at most d of the r - 2 sets {1,b,r} are bad for a family of lists that respects separation.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The minimax theorem for finite matrix games
providers.scope: For a real matrix b: the minimum over laws nu on the rows of the largest column mean equals the maximum over laws rho on the columns of the least row mean. Proved by separating 0 from a closed convex set.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Ramsey's theorem for t-subsets
providers.scope: For t, q, k there is R such that every coloring of the t-subsets of a totally ordered set with at least R elements with q colors has a homogeneous subset with k elements.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Consistent laws of patterns if alignment fails
providers.scope: If for some xi > 0 no r and no law keep the probability of a bad set at most xi for all patterns, there are laws P_t of patterns on [t], consistent under restriction to subsets and renaming in order, with the full set bad with probability at least xi under P_s.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The common index
providers.scope: In the random pattern on the rational numbers built from consistent laws, with probability 1 every label has an element that lies in all of its occurrence sets (its cut, the supremum of the minima of the occurrence sets); so no finite set is bad.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Aligned pairs occur with high probability
providers.scope: With r and the law of B from the alignment theorem for s, d and eps: a chain and a set B fail to be aligned with probability at most 4^r d^2 sigma + eps.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The density bound at an aligned pair
providers.scope: Assume the conditions (P1) to (P6) on the numbers. For an aligned pair of a chain and a set B, the vertex of the experiment lies in a given independent set with conditional probability less than 6 eps.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Hardness of finding large independent sets in three-colorable graphs
providers.scope: Assume the hypotheses (PCP) and (PR). For every 0 < delta < 1/3 there is a polynomial-time map from 3-CNF formulas to graphs: a satisfiable formula gives a graph with a proper coloring with three colors, and a formula that is not satisfiable gives a graph in which every independent set has fewer than delta |V| vertices.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
